questions.stem: What is the site of the TCA cycle?
questions.solutionHtml:
The TCA cycle (Krebs cycle) takes place in the mitochondria. It occurs in all organs of the body.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 156

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Krebs cycle?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins

options.label: B
options.text: Pyruvate condenses with oxaloacetate to form citrate

options.label: C
options.text: Oxidative phosphorylation occurs in the cytoplasm

options.label: D
options.text: Alpha keto glutarate is a 4 carbon compound

questions.answerText: It is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins
questions.solutionHtml:
The Krebs cycle is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins as glucose, fatty acids, and most amino acids are metabolized to acetyl-CoA or intermediates of the cycle.

Other options:

Option B: Acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetate to form citrate.

Option C: Oxidative phosphorylation occurs in mitochondria by ETC (electron transport chain).

Option D: Alpha-ketoglutarate is a 5-carbon compound.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 156, 158

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an intermediate of the TCA cycle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acetyl CoA is not an intermediate formed in the TCA cycle, but rather it is a starting substrate.

There are three sources of acetyl-CoA:

  1. From glucose →Pyruvate → Acetyl-CoA
  2. Fatty acid oxidation → Acetyl-CoA
  3. Ketogenic amino acid oxidation→ acetyl-CoA

The starting materials of Kreb's cycle are Acetyl CoA and oxaloacetic acid. All the other options are intermediates in the TCA cycle and oxaloacetic acid is released in the end.

The image given below depicts the Krebs cycle.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 156, figure 16-2, 16-3

questions.stem: Hyperammonemia inhibits the TCA cycle, by depleting levels of which of the following substances?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hyperammonemia results in the depletion of alpha-ketoglutarate.

This happens in two steps:

  1. The excess free ammonia binds to glutamate and forms glutamine.
  2. To compensate for the reduced glutamate, alpha-ketoglutarate is aminated to glutamate.

Thus, hyperammonemia eventually depletes alpha-ketoglutarate, leading to a stoppage of the TCA cycle.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 156

questions.stem: Aconitase contains which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aconitase is a Fe-containing enzyme. It is involved in the conversion of citrate to isocitrate.

The process occurs as a two-step reaction catalyzed by the enzyme, aconitase.

  1. There is an initial dehydration reaction with the removal of a molecule of water, from Cis-Aconitate.
  2. This is followed up by a rehydration reaction, where a molecule of water is added to Cis-Aconitate, thereby forming Isocitrate.

Note: Aconitase is involved in iron homeostasis.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 31st edition, Pg 151
Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 101

questions.stem: Which of the following substances inhibits aconitase enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flouroacetate is an inhibitor of the aconitase enzyme.

Fluoroacetate combines with Co-A to form fluoroacetyl-CoA. Fluoroacetyl-CoA then condenses with oxaloacetate to form Fluorocitrate. Fluorocitrate then inhibits the enzyme aconitase.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 158

questions.stem: At which level does valine enter the TCA cycle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Valine enters the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) cycle at the succinyl CoA level.

questions.stem: In the Krebs cycle, Which of the following catalyses the step in which the first CO2 is released?
questions.solutionHtml:
Isocitrate dehydrogenase catalyses the step in which the first CO2 is released.

CO2 is released and NAD+ is reduced to NADH in this reaction.

There are two oxidative decarboxylation steps in TCA cycle:

  1. Isocitrate to alpha ketoglutarate catalysed by isocitrate dehydrogenase.
  2. Alpha ketoglutarate to succinyl CoA catalysed by alpha ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 157, Figure 16-2

questions.stem: What is the co-factor needed for the isocitrate dehydrogenase enzyme for decarboxylation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Isocitrate dehydrogenase catalyzes the decarboxylation of isocitrate, to form α-ketoglutarate. This decarboxylation reaction, requires Mg2+ or Mn2+ ions.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 158, figure 16-3

questions.stem: Substrate level phosphorylation occurs in which of the following steps of the TCA cycle?

options.label: B
options.text: Alpha keto glutarate to succinyl CoA

questions.solutionHtml:
Substrate level phosphorylation occurs when succinyl CoA gets converted to succinate in the TCA cycle.

Succinyl-CoA is converted to succinate by the enzyme succinate thiokinase or also called succinyl-CoA synthetase.

GTP formation takes place in this step, and hence this is the one and only example of substrate-level phosphorylation in the TCA cycle.

The GTP so formed is used for the decarboxylation of oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate catalysed by PEPCK in gluconeogenesis.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 157, 158

questions.stem: How many ATPs are generated per turn of the TCA cycle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Total ATPs generated per turn of the TCA cycle is 10.

The following steps of the TCA yield ATP:

  • Isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate – Yields 1 NADH per turn
  • Alpha-ketoglutarate to Succinyl CoA – yields 1 NADH per turn
  • Succinyl Co A to Succinate – yields 1 GTP (Substrate level phosphorylation)
  • Succinate to fumarate – Yields 1 FADH2
  • Malate to Oxaloacetate – Yields 1 NADH

So total ATP formed will be= 10

                            3×NADH=7.5 ATP

                            1× FADH2=1.5 ATP

                            1× GTP= 1 ATP

                            TOTAL= 10 ATP PER TURN





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page no 158

questions.stem: All of the following serve as cofactors for the enzymes of the TCA cycle, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Biotin (B7) is not a cofactor for TCA cycle enzymes.

The following vitamins serve as cofactors for various enzymes of the TCA cycle:

  • Riboflavin (B2)
    • Active form: FAD
    • Cofactor for: Succinate dehydrogenase
  • Niacin (B3)
    • Active form: NAD+
    • Cofactor for: Isocitrate dehydrogenase, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and Malate dehydrogenase complex
  • Thiamine (B1)
    • Active form: Thiamin diphosphate
    • Cofactor for: decarboxylation step of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex
  • Pantothenic acid (B5)
    • Active form: As a part of Coenzyme A
    • Cofactor for: esterified to the carboxylic acid residues, i.e. acetyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 159-160

questions.stem: Why is the TCA cycle called as an amphibolic pathway?

options.label: A
options.text: Both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place

options.label: B
options.text: Metabolites are utilized in other pathways

options.label: C
options.text: It can proceed both in forward and backward direction

options.label: D
options.text: Same enzymes can be used in reverse direction

questions.answerText: Both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place
questions.solutionHtml:
In the TCA cycle, both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place.

The TCA cycle is not only a pathway for oxidation but also that of interconversion of metabolites arising from the transamination and deamination of amino acids. It provides the substrates for amino acid synthesis by transamination as well as for gluconeogenesis and fatty acid synthesis.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 158-159

questions.stem: Which of the following substances inhibit the enzyme alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase in the TCA cycle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arsenite inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

Inhibitors of TCA cycle:

Enzyme Inhibitor
Aconitase Fluoroacetate
Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase Arsenite
Succinate dehydrogenase  Malonate




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 158, figure 16-3

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a cofactor of the enzyme alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyridoxal phosphate is not a cofactor of the enzyme alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase enzyme complex has 5 coenzymes, They are :

  • Lipoate
  • Thiamine pyrophosphate
  • NAD+
  • FAD
  • Coenzyme A

All the enzymes carrying out oxidative decarboxylation require these 5 coenzymes, namely:

  • Pyruvate dehydrogenase, catalyzing the reaction Pyruvate to acetyl CoA
  • Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase
  • Branched-chain keto acid dehydrogenase




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 158, 159

questions.stem: All of the following enzymes are components of the pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme complex, except
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyruvate kinase is not a component of the Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) enzyme complex.

Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is a multienzyme complex that is associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane which catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to Acetyl-CoA.

The three enzyme components are:

  • Pyruvate dehydrogenase
  • Dihydrolipoyl transacetylase
  • Dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase

The Cofactors are:

  • Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)
  • Lipoic acid
  • Coenzyme A
  • Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)
  • Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)

The overall reaction is : Pyruvate + NAD+ + CoA → Acetyl-CoA + NADH + H+ + CO2



Clinical aspects:

  • Arsenite and mercuric ions react with the -SH groups of lipoic acid and inhibit pyruvate dehydrogenase.
  • Dietary deficiency of thiamin inhibits PDH eg. Chronic alcoholics may develop potentially fatal pyruvic and lactic acidosis.
  • Patients with inherited pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency present with lactic acidosis, particularly after a glucose load and neurological disturbances.

Note : Pyruvate kinase catalyses the last step of glycolysis ie- transfering phosphate group from phosphoenol pyruvate to ADP forming pyruvate and ATP respectively. 





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, pg 169

questions.stem: Which of the following is inhibited in thiamine deficiency?
questions.solutionHtml:
In thiamine deficiency, conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA is inhibited.

Thiamine is a cofactor of the pyruvate dehydrogenase component of the PDH complex. In thiamine deficiency, pyruvate dehydrogenase is inhibited. Hence pyruvate is not converted to acetyl CoA.

Other options:

Option A: The enzyme involved in converting isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate is isocitrate dehydrogenase which requires Mn2+or Mg2+ as a co-factor.

Option B: Riboflavin (FAD) is the co-factor for succinate dehydrogenase enzyme, which is responsible for converting succinate to fumarate.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 169-170

questions.stem: Which of the following is an allosteric inhibitor of pyruvate dehydrogenase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Allosteric inhibitors of the PDH enzyme complex are NADH, acetyl CoA, and ATP.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 168

questions.stem: Which of the following enzyme deficiencies is likely to cause congenital lactic acidosis in a patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inherited pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, can be due to a defect in any one/ more of the components of the PDH enzyme complex. This presents with lactic acidosis.

Causes of lactic acidosis:

  1. Tissue hypoxia
  2. Mitochondrial disorders
  3. Deficiency of:   
    • PDH  Enzyme
    • TCA cycle enzymes
    • Vit B1
  4. Poisoning:
    • Cyanide 
    • Mercury
    • Arsenite




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 169-170

questions.stem: Identify the anaplerotic reaction among the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Conversion of pyruvate to Acetyl CoA

options.label: D
options.text: Conversion of pyruvate to Lactic acid

questions.solutionHtml:
The conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate is an anaplerotic reaction. It is catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase.

Anaplerotic reactions are chemical reactions that form intermediates of a metabolic pathway. The above reaction is important in maintaining an adequate concentration of oxaloacetate for the condensation reaction with acetyl-CoA. If acetyl-CoA accumulates, it acts as an activator of pyruvate carboxylase and an inhibitor of pyruvate dehydrogenase, thereby ensuring an adequate supply of oxaloacetate.

Other anaplerotic reactions are:

  • Compounds that are metabolized to yield propionyl CoA, which can be then carboxylated and isomerized to succinyl CoA.
  • Glutamate and glutamine are important anaplerotic substrates because they yield α-ketoglutarate as a result of the reactions catalyzed by glutaminase and glutamate dehydrogenase.
  • Transamination of aspartate leads directly to the formation of oxaloacetate.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 160
